the effects of R+ and Rb+ on the inward rectifier K channel are due to (1) a cooperative process of plugging the pore that is associated with a slowing of isomerization rates and a decrease in the binding affinity of allosterically acting K+ ions on the outside of open channels, and (2) an increase in affinity of allostericaly acting K+ ions that promote channel opening.
the inward rectifier K channel of bovine artery endothe- lial cells is a triple-barreled, electrochemically gated, allosteric channel that is modulated by Rb+ and other activator ions.
